analyzed_vuln.description: `Crypto::decode_pem(ReadonlyBytes)` logs an error with `dbgln("Failed to decode PEM, likely bad Base64")` when Base64 decoding fails. In this fuzz target/build configuration, that formatting/logging path invokes AK formatting with a corrupted/invalid zero-parameter pack state (`VariadicFormatParams<>::set_parameters` on `Array<...,0>`), producing UB reported in `AK/Format.h:269`. For this PoV, the actionable root cause is that `decode_pem` reaches the error logging path on malformed PEM/Base64 input without guarding against this sanitizer-exposed formatting edge case.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Harness `FuzzPEM` directly passes attacker-controlled bytes to `Crypto::decode_pem`. Input that contains a `-----BEGIN` line and then a non-empty, non-base64 payload line (PoC: `"-----BEGIN\n "`) causes `decode_base64(...)` to return no value, which triggers the `dbgln(...)` error path and then UB in AK format machinery. So trigger requires malformed PEM body that forces the bad-Base64 branch in `decode_pem`.
